title: Tenant fractionalization and burst fallbacks proposal
creator: Ava Santiago
description: Summary: After the March 2026 capacity incident (large eviction spike in dedicated-gpu pools) we observed correlated noisy-tenant behavior where several mid-size tenants consumed transient working sets that exceeded their reserved footprint and then burst tokens overwhelmed the soft-burst policy. Root cause hypothesis: a combination of under-provisioned fractional reservations for bursty inference patterns, lack of a short-window noisy-tenant detector, and an overly-permissive burst fallback that allowed a small group of tenants to amplify token allocation under steady-state load. Goal: implement lightweight tenant fractionalization (pro-rate reservation model for short-lived high-fanout requests), add an early noisy neighbor quarantine detector, and tighten burst fallback policies with graceful degradation and quota rebalancing to prevent cascade evictions.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy noisy-tenant detector with false-positive rate < 2% on the validation cluster
New fractional reservation mode reduces eviction rate in synthetic burst tests by >= 60%
Burst fallback policy enforces per-tenant degrade path (latency-first) and prevents more than one downstream eviction per incident window
Telemetry dashboard shows tenant-level KV cache miss rate, short-window token burn, and synthetic-simulated mitigation results
Runbook updated with step-by-step quarantine and recovery flow; on-call can run automated mitigation in under 6 minutes
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype fractional reservations: implement pro-rata reservation layer that allocates a transient fractional credit pool (owner: Ravi) - RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/proto/pull/876

2) Detector: integrate short-window noisy-tenant detector using 30s rolling token burn and KV miss rate (owner: Mei Chen) - feature branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/noisy-detector

3) Burst fallback rewrite: change fallback path to favor per-request latency degradation over global burst assignment. Implement graded token throttling and fallback to smaller quantized model when necessary (owner: Carlos Dominguez)
4) Telemetry: add per-tenant panels and alerting for short-window token burn > X and eviction spike probability > Y (owner: DataInfra)
5) Canary: run in dedicated-lab with synthetic tenants at 3x baseline for 72h, iterate on thresholds, then staged rollout to 10% of clusters
6) Post-deploy: 48h runbook drill and follow-up incident review (owner: On-call)
Estimated work breakdown: 3 devs (2w), 1 SRE (1w), 1 data engineer (1w)
telemetry_changes: Dashboard: Dedicated -> Tenant Stability -> Fractionalization Canary
Alert: P0 if eviction_rate_cluster > 0.5% AND top-5 tenants account for > 60% short_window_token_burn
runbook_changes: Add step: 'Detect noisy tenant' with query and automated action to place tenant in quarantine-cgroup
Add step: 'Apply fractional reservation' for suspected tenants to prevent global burst exhaustion
Add step: 'Escalation' to capacity-engineering Slack channel and attach synthetic load artifacts
Recovery checklist: how to revert fractional mode and rollback fallback changes
risks: False positives in detector could throttle legitimate traffic - mitigated by conservative initial thresholds and manual review flag
Fractional reservations may increase latency for legitimate large-batch jobs; we'll provide an opt-out path for enterprise tenants via reservation override
Complexity in burst fallback increases operator surface area - mitigate with end-to-end tests and observability
